title: What shape is the shadow of a tilted square card?
description: A square card with diagonals of ten centimetres is tilted in sunlight about one diagonal. The board follows the two diagonals of the shadow, names the shape they make, and uses the theorem of Ziva on the half diagonals to find each side. Keeko's doubt is that the shadow is still a square.
teaching_notes: One idea: a shadow keeps parallel lines parallel, so the shadow of the card is a parallelogram, and diagonals that cross at right angles make it a rhombus. Watch for students who think the shadow of a square is always a square.

source: A square card has diagonals of 10 cm. It is tilted in sunlig
video_script.why: The child names the shape of a shadow from its diagonals and finds a side from the half diagonals.
video_script.substitution: Side = square root of (half of one diagonal squared + half of the other squared).
video_script.anchor: a square card tilted in sunlight about one diagonal, with its shadow drawn on the ground
video_script.wrong_answer: the shadow is still a square
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the shadow is still a square because the card is a square. The shadow diagonals are ten and six centimetres, and a square has two diagonals of the same length.
video_script.payoff_line: The shadow is a rhombus, and each side is about five point eight three centimetres

final_answer.value: a rhombus, each side about 5.83 cm
final_answer.spoken: a rhombus, and each side is about five point eight three centimetres

names.Ziva: the theorem used for the shortest path of 40 cm

hold_back: Answer: a rhombus, each side about 5.83 cm
never_show: a square shadow marked as right
maths_rules: the card is a square with both diagonals 10 cm
tilted about one diagonal: that diagonal stays 10 cm; the shadow of the other diagonal is 6 cm
the shadow diagonals cross at their middles at right angles; opposite sides stay parallel, so the shadow is a rhombus
side = square root of 34 = 5.83 cm (5.83 x 5.83 = 33.99, about 34)
slip: the shadow is still a square, which needs equal diagonals
video_script.design: The tilted card and its shadow on the stage. The shadow's two diagonals are drawn and labelled, then one right triangle of half diagonals is lifted out for the side.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the shadow of a card.
<bookmark mark='card'/>A square card has diagonals of ten centimetres.
<bookmark mark='tilt'/>It is tilted in sunlight about one diagonal. The shadow of the other diagonal is six centimetres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What shape is the shadow, and how long is each side?

marks.par: two parallel sides of the card and their shadows glow
marks.para: the shadow outline is shaded as a parallelogram
marks.hinge: the diagonal we tilt about is marked along the ground

narration: <bookmark mark='par'/>The shadow of two parallel lines stays two parallel lines.
<bookmark mark='para'/>That makes the shadow of a square card a parallelogram.
<bookmark mark='hinge'/>The diagonal we tilt about lies along the ground, and it keeps its length.

beats.on_screen: Given: square card, both diagonals 10 cm; tilted about one diagonal; shadow of the other diagonal 6 cm

marks.given: the card, the tilt and the two lengths are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the card is a square with diagonals of ten centimetres.
It is tilted about one diagonal, and the other diagonal casts a shadow of six centimetres.

beats.on_screen: To find: the shape of the shadow and the length of each side

marks.find: the words shape and side are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the shape of the shadow and the length of each side.

marks.diag: the two shadow diagonals are drawn and labelled 10 cm and 6 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='diag'/>Step one, write the two diagonals of the shadow.
The diagonal we tilt about stays ten centimetres. The other shadow diagonal is six centimetres.

beats.on_screen: The shadow diagonals cross at their middles at right angles. A parallelogram with diagonals at right angles is a rhombus.

marks.cross: the two diagonals cross and a right angle mark appears at the middle
marks.name: the shadow is shaded and labelled rhombus

narration: <bookmark mark='cross'/>Step two, name the shape. The shadow diagonals still cross at their middles, at right angles.
That is because the tilt is about one diagonal.
<bookmark mark='name'/>A parallelogram with diagonals at right angles is a rhombus.

beats.on_screen: Half diagonals: 10 / 2 = 5 cm and 6 / 2 = 3 cm. side squared = 5 x 5 + 3 x 3 = 25 + 9 = 34

marks.half: a right triangle with sides 5 cm and 3 cm is lifted out of the rhombus
marks.sq: side squared = 5 x 5 + 3 x 3 = 25 + 9 = 34 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>Step three, use the theorem of Ziva. Half of each diagonal gives a right triangle, with sides of five and three centimetres.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>The side of the rhombus is the long side of that triangle.
Five squared plus three squared is twenty five plus nine, which is thirty four.

beats.on_screen: side = square root of 34 = about 5.83 cm. Check: 5.83 x 5.83 is about 34

marks.root: side = square root of 34 = about 5.83 cm is written
marks.check: 5.83 x 5.83 is about 34 is written under it

narration: <bookmark mark='root'/>Step four, take the square root. The side is the square root of thirty four, about five point eight three centimetres.
<bookmark mark='check'/>To check, five point eight three times five point eight three is about thirty four.

beats.on_screen: Answer: a rhombus, each side about 5.83 cm
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The shadow is a rhombus, and each side is about five point eight three centimetres.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the shadow is still a square, because the card is a square.
<bookmark mark='lay'/>But a square has two diagonals of the same length.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The shadow diagonals are ten and six centimetres, so the shadow cannot be a square.
